author_notes: Slot slot_163 targets the runnable cullenwebber three-html-to-canvas Vite/Three.js demo, whose visible motion is driven by a local public/model.glb asset projected from an offscreen DOM raster. The native lever is the demo's own on-canvas Projection console (#proj-console): a control panel floating over the fixed WebGL canvas that names the real local pipeline assets (offscreen #page raster, CanvasTexture source, ProjectedMaterial on model.glb, Lenis scroll camera) in a four-tile status strip and lets the visitor pick which projection stage the console is inspecting. The reference console is legible and responsive, its stage selector rewrites the live readout on every pick, and it persists across the scroll-driven camera path. The baseline shares the broken tile CSS (a fixed-width flex-nowrap track of oversized cascading near-black slabs that overlap and overflow on mobile) and the entry-only presence bug, but its stage selector still updates the readout correctly. The known-bad leg adds a frozen readout so picking a stage moves the highlight but leaves the console reporting the wrong stage. The local projected assets (model.glb, draco, fonts), the WebGL scene, the HtmlToCanvas raster, ProjectedMaterial, and the Lenis scroll camera are identical across all three legs and are preserved; only the console's layout CSS, its readout wiring, and its cross-context presence whitelist differ. Screenshots, svg/image assets and the model.glb mesh continuity are checked alongside no-horizontal-overflow, visual regression, cross-context DOM presence, and the stage-selector interaction.
design_constraints: Preserve the white minimal Three.js projection scene, the full-viewport fixed WebGL canvas, scroll-driven camera motion, Geist typography, the bright red (#fd453a) accent, and the local public/model.glb asset.

Keep the Projection console as a native on-canvas control panel naming the real local pipeline assets (offscreen #page DOM raster, CanvasTexture source, ProjectedMaterial on model.glb, Lenis scroll camera).

Repair the console tile layout so it reflows on narrow viewports, stays legible (no near-black-on-near-black text, no overlapping slabs burying the scene), and produces no horizontal overflow on a 390px mobile viewport (tolerance 24px).
Wire the projection-stage selector so clicking a stage rewrites the live readout to that stage; the active highlight and the readout must agree.
Keep the console layered above the canvas and present across the scroll-driven camera path without hiding the central 3D model in the mid-scroll and deep-scroll states.
Do not remove the local projected assets (public/model.glb, public/draco, public/fonts) or replace the WebGL scene with static screenshots, remote media, or a detached documentation page.
Preserve the existing Three.js architecture: Scene loads model.glb, HtmlToCanvas rasterizes #page, ProjectedMaterial maps the texture, and Lenis scroll remains the camera driver.

The console stays present across the entry, mid-scroll, and deep-scroll camera contexts so the pipeline guide is continuous.
responsive: The console status tiles reflow into a wrapped column on narrow viewports instead of a fixed-width track.
No horizontal overflow on a 390px mobile viewport (tolerance 24px) across initial and scrolled states.
regression: The white Three.js projection scene, the fixed full-viewport WebGL canvas, model.glb, and Lenis scroll motion remain intact.
The console tiles remain legible (no near-black-on-near-black text, no overlapping slabs) rather than burying the scene.

metadata.source_repo_kind: Vite Three.js WebGL projection demo with offscreen HTML source, local model.glb, ProjectedMaterial, HtmlToCanvas, Lenis scroll, and Tailwind CSS.

problem_statement: The three-html-to-canvas Vite/Three.js demo projects an offscreen DOM page onto a local model by rasterizing #page through HtmlToCanvas into a CanvasTexture and applying it with ProjectedMaterial while a Lenis scroll loop drives the camera. A native on-canvas Projection console floats over the full-viewport fixed WebGL surface: it names the real local pipeline assets in a four-tile status strip (DOM raster #page, CanvasTexture source, ProjectedMaterial on model.glb, the Lenis scroll camera) and lets the visitor pick which projection STAGE the console is inspecting (Full pipeline / DOM raster / CanvasTexture / Projected mesh), updating a live readout beneath the selector. Three defects were introduced together and must all be repaired: (1) the console's tile track regressed to an oversized fixed-width flex-nowrap row whose slabs cascade with negative margins so they overlap, bury the scene, and render their labels near-black on near-black (illegible), and on a 390px mobile viewport the track spills past the screen edge (horizontal overflow); (2) picking a stage only moves the active-tab highlight while the readout stays frozen on 'Full pipeline', so the console reports the wrong stage; (3) the console is only wired for the entry view and disappears once the Lenis camera scrolls into the mid and deep segments of the path instead of persisting across it. Restore a legible, responsive console whose tiles reflow (no horizontal overflow on mobile, tolerance 24px), whose stage selector rewrites the live readout on every pick, and which stays present across the scroll-driven camera path, while keeping the offscreen #page projection source, the local model.glb, the full-screen WebGL scene, the Lenis scroll motion, and the Vite/Three.js architecture intact. Do not remove the local projected assets or replace the canvas with a static screenshot or unrelated landing page.
required_content: Keep the on-canvas Projection console naming the real local pipeline assets: DOM raster on #page, the CanvasTexture source, ProjectedMaterial on model.glb, and the Lenis scroll camera.
Repair the console's tile layout so the status tiles reflow legibly (no overlapping dark-on-dark slabs) and produce no horizontal overflow on a 390px mobile viewport.
Make the projection-stage selector rewrite the live readout on every pick (Full pipeline / DOM raster / CanvasTexture / Projected mesh), not just move the active highlight.
Keep the Projection console present across the Lenis scroll-driven camera path (entry, mid-scroll, and deep-scroll), not only on the entry view.
Keep the offscreen #page source feeding the projected CanvasTexture; do not remove it or substitute a raster image.
Preserve the local public/model.glb load path, the local draco decoders, Scene.js projection setup, HtmlToCanvas utility, ProjectedMaterial utility, and Lenis scroll behavior.
Desktop, tablet, and mobile initial states plus scrolled canvas states must remain responsive without horizontal overflow.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial protect the first viewport and verify that the Projection console is legible and does not overflow before scrolling.
desktop_console is the desktop console-in-frame state used for visible-text and visual-regression checks over the console panel and its status tiles.
mobile_console verifies the console reflows without horizontal overflow on a 390px viewport.
desktop_stage_pick clicks a projection-stage button and checks that the live readout updates to the selected stage (catches a frozen readout).
desktop_mid_scroll and desktop_deep_scroll protect the scroll-driven 3D model view and verify the console persists across the Lenis camera path.
mobile_scroll verifies responsiveness of the scrolled canvas state on mobile.
